solo operator.first_week: Batch admin into one named window and protect one delivery block outside it.
solo operator.week_shape: Delivery, admin, and sales interleave all week, and the interleaving costs more than any one of them.
solo operator.protect: One uninterrupted delivery block per day, with admin batched outside it.
solo operator.advice_that_fails: "Use a better tool." Every switch discards the accumulated state that made the last tool useful.
solo operator.vignette: The delivery block started at 09:00 and it is now 09:25, because an invoice query arrived and answering it felt like two minutes. The delivery work has not been reopened since.

executive.context: Most of your calendar is committed by other people and the residue is where your own work has to fit.
executive.constraint: Contiguous time. The gaps between meetings are numerous and none of them is long enough.
executive.hardest: Doing anything that requires more than twenty-five uninterrupted minutes.
executive.scene: an executive with a day of thirty-minute gaps and one decision that needs an hour
executive.mistaken_for: Needing more time. The calendar is not going to yield; the residue has to be used differently.
executive.wrong_metric: Meeting count. Removing meetings is rarely available; using the gaps is.
executive.first_week: Match work to gap length in advance so a thirty-minute window never gets a task that needs ninety.
executive.week_shape: A calendar filled by other people, with your own work living in the residue between commitments.
executive.protect: One ninety-minute block a week that nothing is allowed to book over.
executive.advice_that_fails: "Take fewer meetings." Usually unavailable, and it treats the symptom rather than how the gaps get used.
executive.vignette: The calendar shows six meetings with twenty-five-minute gaps between them. The decision that actually matters this week needs an uninterrupted hour, and no such hour exists between now and Thursday.

creative.context: Output quality varies with state more than with hours, and the state is not reliably schedulable.
creative.constraint: Usable creative state, which arrives unpredictably and is spent quickly.
creative.hardest: Producing on a schedule without the schedule flattening the work.
creative.scene: a creative with a deadline and three days of unusable state behind them
creative.mistaken_for: A discipline problem. State-dependent output is a scheduling problem, not a character one.
creative.wrong_metric: Words or pieces per day, which punishes the days spent on the part that is genuinely hard.
creative.first_week: Separate generative work from finishing work in the schedule and stop asking one block to do both.
creative.week_shape: Uneven. Two days can produce more than the other five, and which two is not knowable in advance.
creative.protect: The generative block, kept separate from the finishing block so neither has to be both.
creative.advice_that_fails: "Just show up every day." It works for the finishing half and flattens the generative half.
creative.vignette: Three days have produced nothing usable and the deadline is in four. The temptation is to work longer today, which is what produced the three days.

student.context: Deadlines are external and distant, which means nothing is urgent until everything is.
student.constraint: Structure. Nobody is checking in until the deadline, and by then the check-in is a grade.
student.hardest: Starting work whose deadline is far enough away to feel optional.
student.scene: a student three weeks from a deadline with nothing started
student.mistaken_for: Procrastination. It is usually the absence of any check-in between now and the deadline.
student.wrong_metric: Hours studied, which measures presence rather than what exists afterwards.
student.first_week: Set one self-imposed checkpoint per week with something that has to exist at it.
student.week_shape: Flat until a deadline is close, then vertical. The flat part is where the whole outcome is decided.
student.protect: One weekly checkpoint with something that has to exist at it.
student.advice_that_fails: "Manage your time better." There is plenty of time; there is no signal until the deadline.
student.vignette: The deadline is nineteen days away, nothing has been started, and nothing will feel urgent for another twelve days. There is no check-in between now and the grade.

career switcher.context: The work that matters is unpaid and competes with work that is paid and immediate.
career switcher.constraint: Evening and weekend hours, which are also the hours when capacity is lowest.
career switcher.hardest: Keeping the switch alive across weeks where the current job takes everything.
career switcher.scene: a career switcher with two free evenings and a portfolio piece unstarted
career switcher.mistaken_for: Needing more commitment. The hours are genuinely contested and the commitment is usually not the missing part.
career switcher.wrong_metric: Progress compared to someone doing this full time, which is a comparison that only demoralises.
career switcher.first_week: Fix two named evenings and defend them the way you would defend a paid commitment.
career switcher.week_shape: A full week of paid work with two or three contested evenings attached to the end of it.
career switcher.protect: Two named evenings, defended the way a paid commitment would be.
career switcher.advice_that_fails: "Want it more." The hours are genuinely contested and wanting does not create them.
career switcher.vignette: Two evenings this week were free in theory. One went to a work escalation and the other to being too tired to open the laptop. The portfolio piece is where it was in March.

busy parent.context: The day is interrupted by obligations that cannot be rescheduled or delegated.
busy parent.constraint: Predictability. The hours exist but you cannot know in advance which ones.
busy parent.hardest: Any plan that assumes a block will survive to its end.
busy parent.scene: a parent whose only reliable block is forty minutes after bedtime
busy parent.mistaken_for: Needing to get up earlier. Adding hours to an unpredictable day does not make it predictable.
busy parent.wrong_metric: Uninterrupted hours, which for this reader is a number that will not improve.
busy parent.first_week: Design the work around blocks that can be interrupted and resumed, and write the resume point every time you stop.
busy parent.week_shape: Predictable obligations at unpredictable times, and any block can end without notice.
busy parent.protect: The ability to resume: a written stopping point every time you stop.
busy parent.advice_that_fails: "Wake up earlier." Adding hours to an unpredictable day does not make it predictable.
busy parent.vignette: The reliable block is forty minutes after bedtime, and roughly one night in three it does not happen at all. Every plan written so far has assumed the block survives to its end.

consultant.context: Client work is billable and visible; your own business development is neither.
consultant.constraint: Non-billable hours, which are the first thing sacrificed when a client escalates.
consultant.hardest: Doing pipeline work during a busy delivery month, which is when it matters most.
consultant.scene: a consultant fully booked this month with an empty pipeline next month
consultant.mistaken_for: A sales problem. It is usually a scheduling problem: pipeline work has no protected slot.
consultant.wrong_metric: Utilization, which is highest in the month before the pipeline runs dry.
consultant.first_week: Put one recurring non-billable block in the calendar and treat it as booked.
consultant.week_shape: Billable work expands to fill the week, and everything that is not billable happens in the gaps that are left.
consultant.protect: One recurring non-billable block, treated as booked and defended the way a client hour would be.
consultant.advice_that_fails: "Do business development when you have time." That time arrives the month after you needed it.
consultant.vignette: This month is fully booked and next month has two prospects, both cold. The billable work is visible in the calendar and the pipeline work is not in it at all.

sales leader.context: The day is reactive by design: deals, escalations, and a team that needs answers now.
sales leader.constraint: Any time not claimed by someone else, which is very little of it.
sales leader.hardest: Doing the pipeline analysis that would reduce the escalations that prevent the analysis.
sales leader.scene: a sales leader with an unread forecast and four escalations before lunch
sales leader.mistaken_for: Needing to be more responsive. Responsiveness is already maximal and is the thing crowding out the analysis.
sales leader.wrong_metric: Response time, which improves as the underlying problem gets worse.
sales leader.first_week: Take the first block of the day off the queue and give it to the analysis that reduces the queue.
sales leader.week_shape: Reactive by design. Almost every hour is claimable by a deal, an escalation, or a person.
sales leader.protect: The first block of the day, taken off the queue entirely.
sales leader.advice_that_fails: "Be more responsive." Responsiveness is already maximal and is what crowds out the analysis.
sales leader.vignette: Four escalations landed before ten. The forecast has not been read, and reading it is what would reduce next week's escalations.

agency owner.context: You are managing delivery, clients, and a team, and each of the three thinks it is the priority.
agency owner.constraint: Attention split three ways, with each way expanding to fill whatever it gets.
agency owner.hardest: Working on the agency rather than in it, on a day where in-it is on fire.
agency owner.scene: an agency owner with a client escalation and an unwritten hiring plan
agency owner.mistaken_for: Needing more capacity. Three competing demands do not resolve by adding people to one of them.
agency owner.wrong_metric: Client satisfaction alone, which stays high right up to the point the agency has no plan.
agency owner.first_week: Name which of delivery, clients, or the business owns each block before the week starts.
agency owner.week_shape: Three competing claims - delivery, clients, and the business - and each expands to fill whatever it gets.
agency owner.protect: A named owner for each block before the week starts.
agency owner.advice_that_fails: "Hire someone." It adds capacity to one of the three claims and leaves the arbitration unchanged.
agency owner.vignette: A client is unhappy, a delivery deadline is Thursday, and the hiring plan has been open in a tab since last month. Each of the three is convinced it is today's priority.

builder.context: Building is the enjoyable part, and everything that turns building into a business is not.
builder.constraint: Willingness to do the non-building work, which is scarcer than the hours.
builder.hardest: Stopping a build to do the distribution work that would make the build matter.
builder.scene: a builder on version four of a product nobody has used
builder.mistaken_for: Needing to build something better. Version four of an unused product is not a build problem.
builder.wrong_metric: Features shipped, which can go up indefinitely without a single user.
builder.first_week: Spend the first block of every day on something that is not building, and record what it produced.
builder.week_shape: Building fills the week comfortably; everything that turns building into a business does not.
builder.protect: One daily block for work that is not building, however small.
builder.advice_that_fails: "Build something people want." True and unactionable while the week contains no non-building time.
builder.vignette: Version four is nearly ready. Versions one to three were also nearly ready, and nobody outside the team has used any of them.

high performer.context: The current standard is being sustained by effort, and effort is a resource with a limit.
high performer.constraint: Recovery. Output is fine and the margin behind it is thinner than it looks.
high performer.hardest: Reducing anything, because everything is currently working.
high performer.scene: a high performer whose output is fine and whose margin has been gone for a month
high performer.mistaken_for: Being fine. Output is the last thing to fall, so it is the worst early indicator available.
high performer.wrong_metric: Current output, which is exactly the number that will look good until it does not.
high performer.first_week: Write down what your margin actually is right now, and what would happen next week if one thing went wrong.
high performer.boundary: If the honest answer involves your health, that is a conversation with a qualified professional rather than a scheduling change.
high performer.week_shape: Full and functioning, with no visible slack and no visible problem until something goes wrong.
high performer.protect: The margin, which is the thing that disappears first and is noticed last.
high performer.advice_that_fails: "You're doing fine." Output is the last indicator to fall, so it is the worst early warning available.
high performer.vignette: Output this quarter is the best it has been. The margin behind it went two months ago, and nothing has gone wrong yet, which is the only reason it still looks fine.

manager.context: Your output is produced by other people, and your own tasks compete with unblocking theirs.
manager.constraint: Uninterrupted time, which is structurally at odds with being available.
manager.hardest: Deciding when unblocking someone should wait.
manager.scene: a manager with two people blocked and one report due
manager.mistaken_for: Needing to delegate more. The unblocking work is the job; the question is when it can wait.
manager.wrong_metric: Availability, which is easy to maximize and directly opposed to your own deliverables.
manager.first_week: Declare two response windows and hold your own block outside them.
manager.week_shape: Split between your own deliverables and unblocking other people, with no boundary between the two.
manager.protect: Two declared response windows, with your own block outside them.
manager.advice_that_fails: "Be available." Availability is easy to maximize and directly opposed to your own output.
manager.vignette: Two people have been blocked since Tuesday and a report is due tomorrow. Unblocking them takes ninety minutes; the report takes the same ninety minutes.

freelancer.context: Income tracks hours delivered, so anything not delivered is visibly unpaid.
freelancer.constraint: Money-time, which makes every non-billable hour feel like a decision about rent.
freelancer.hardest: Investing time in anything with a payoff further out than the next invoice.
freelancer.scene: a freelancer with a slow month and no time set aside for finding the next client
freelancer.mistaken_for: Needing more clients. Usually there is no protected time for finding them, which is a different fix.
freelancer.wrong_metric: Billable hours this week, which is highest in the weeks you are doing nothing about next month.
freelancer.first_week: Book one non-billable block for client-finding and treat it as a client commitment.
freelancer.week_shape: Billable when work exists and structureless when it does not, which is when structure matters most.
freelancer.protect: One non-billable block for finding the next client, treated as a client commitment.
freelancer.advice_that_fails: "Raise your rates." Sometimes right, and it does nothing about the empty week after this one.
freelancer.vignette: This week is quiet, which means unpaid, which makes it the worst week to spend a day on finding the next client and the only week it is possible.

startup operator.context: Priorities are reset frequently from above and each reset invalidates part of the current plan.
startup operator.constraint: Plan stability, which is genuinely outside your control.
startup operator.hardest: Making a week-long plan when the week's priority may change on Wednesday.
startup operator.scene: a startup operator on the third priority reset this month
startup operator.mistaken_for: Needing a better plan. Plans are being invalidated from above, which no plan quality fixes.
startup operator.wrong_metric: Plan adherence, which measures something outside your control.
startup operator.first_week: Plan at day level with a stable weekly floor, so a Wednesday reset costs one day rather than the week.
startup operator.week_shape: Planned on Monday and invalidated by Wednesday, repeatedly and for reasons outside your control.
startup operator.protect: A stable daily floor, so a mid-week reset costs a day rather than the week.
startup operator.advice_that_fails: "Plan better." No plan quality survives priorities being reset from above.
startup operator.vignette: Monday's plan was invalidated on Wednesday for the third time this month. Two days of the week's work is now irrelevant and the week is still expected to deliver.

creator.context: Publishing cadence is the thing that compounds and the thing that slips first.
creator.constraint: A repeatable production floor, as distinct from the ability to make a good piece.
creator.hardest: Publishing on the weeks the work is not your best.
creator.scene: a creator two weeks past their own publishing cadence
creator.mistaken_for: A quality problem. The cadence usually breaks on the weeks the work is ordinary, not the weeks it is bad.
creator.wrong_metric: Engagement on the last piece, which varies for reasons unrelated to whether you publish next week.
creator.first_week: Define the floor version of a publishable piece and publish that on the next ordinary week.
creator.week_shape: Production and publishing on a cadence, with the cadence breaking on the ordinary weeks rather than the bad ones.
creator.protect: The floor version of a publishable piece, defined before you need it.
creator.advice_that_fails: "Only publish your best work." It sounds like standards and functions as a reason not to publish.
creator.vignette: The piece for this week is fine rather than good. The cadence has held for eleven weeks and the temptation to skip one is entirely about the word fine.

investor.context: Inbound volume is high and the cost of a missed good opportunity is invisible.
investor.constraint: Screening capacity. Everything can be looked at; only some things can be looked at properly.
investor.hardest: Saying no fast enough to leave time to say yes properly.
investor.scene: an investor with forty unscreened inbounds and two live processes
investor.mistaken_for: Needing to see more. Screening capacity is the constraint, and more inbound makes it worse.
investor.wrong_metric: Deals seen, which rewards volume over the depth that actually decides outcomes.
investor.first_week: Write the two-line no criteria and apply them before anything reaches a real read.
investor.week_shape: Continuous inbound with two or three live processes competing for the same deep attention.
investor.protect: Screening capacity, by saying no fast enough to leave room to say yes properly.
investor.advice_that_fails: "See more deals." More inbound against fixed screening capacity makes the problem worse.
investor.vignette: Forty inbounds are unscreened and two live processes need a real read this week. Everything in the forty can be looked at; only a few can be looked at properly.

team lead.context: You still do the work and you are also responsible for the team's output.
team lead.constraint: Role clarity within your own day. Both jobs are real and neither is scheduled.
team lead.hardest: Knowing which of the two roles a given hour belongs to.
team lead.scene: a team lead with their own deliverable and a team member stuck since Tuesday
team lead.mistaken_for: Needing to choose between the two roles. Both are real; what is missing is which hour belongs to which.
team lead.wrong_metric: Personal output, which for this role is only half the job and the easier half to measure.
team lead.first_week: Label each block as own-work or team-work before the day starts, and keep the labels.
team lead.week_shape: Two jobs sharing one calendar, with neither of them scheduled as such.
team lead.protect: A label on every block: own-work or team-work, decided before the day starts.
team lead.advice_that_fails: "Focus on the team." It is half the job, and dropping the other half is not available.
team lead.vignette: The morning went to unblocking, the afternoon was supposed to go to their own deliverable, and an hour of it went to a question that could have waited.

researcher.context: The work has long feedback cycles, so progress is hard to see day to day.
researcher.constraint: Evidence of movement, which is what sustains work over months.
researcher.hardest: Maintaining a daily practice against a payoff measured in quarters.
researcher.scene: a researcher four months into a project with nothing publishable yet
researcher.mistaken_for: A motivation problem. Long feedback cycles remove the daily signal that sustains most practices.
researcher.wrong_metric: Publications, which are quarters away and cannot tell you whether this week went well.
researcher.first_week: Record one line of evidence per day of what moved, so the week has a signal of its own.
researcher.week_shape: Long, undifferentiated, with the payoff far enough away to give no weekly signal.
researcher.protect: A daily line of evidence, so the week has a signal of its own.
researcher.advice_that_fails: "Stay motivated." Motivation is downstream of signal, and there is no signal at this timescale.
researcher.vignette: Four months in with nothing publishable. Every individual week looks identical from the inside, which is why the fourth month feels like the first.

coach.context: Your own system is the thing you teach, and it is the thing you run last.
coach.constraint: Attention for your own practice after a day of giving it to other people.
coach.hardest: Applying to yourself, at the end of the day, what you applied to clients all day.
coach.scene: a coach who has run six sessions and not opened their own review
coach.mistaken_for: Not practicing what you teach. The material is fine; it is scheduled last, which is a different problem.
coach.wrong_metric: Client outcomes, which say nothing about whether your own practice is running.
coach.first_week: Put your own review before the first session of the day rather than after the last.
coach.week_shape: Sessions all day, with your own practice scheduled after the last one and therefore not happening.
coach.protect: Your own review, moved to before the first session rather than after the last.
coach.advice_that_fails: "Practice what you teach." You know the material; it is scheduled last, which is a different problem.
coach.vignette: Six sessions today, each of them spent applying a structure to somebody else's week. Their own review has not been opened since the previous Friday.

habit tracker.does_well: Records whether a repeated action happened, and makes the record visible over time.
habit tracker.does_not: Decides nothing. It has no view on which action is worth repeating or what to do on the day you miss.
habit tracker.choose_when: The action is already correct and settled, and the only missing piece is the record.
habit tracker.differs: A tracker measures a system. It is not one, and treating it as one is why trackers get abandoned around the third missed day.
habit tracker.mistaken_for: A system. It is an instrument that measures one.
habit tracker.wrong_metric: Streak length, which says nothing about what happens after a break.
habit tracker.first_week: Keep the tracker and add one written rule for the day after a miss.
habit tracker.stack: Use the tracker as the record and put the decision about what to do on a missed day somewhere else.

planner.does_well: Holds a plan in a fixed layout, which makes the plan visible and reduces the cost of remembering it.
planner.does_not: Check whether the plan fits the hours available, or say what happens when it does not.
planner.choose_when: You already produce plans that fit and need somewhere stable to put them.
planner.differs: A planner accepts any plan, including an impossible one. The arithmetic that makes a plan possible happens before the planner.
planner.mistaken_for: A plan. It is a place to hold one, and it accepts impossible ones.
planner.wrong_metric: How full the page looks at the start of the day.
planner.first_week: Write the workable-hours number in the planner before the tasks.
planner.stack: Keep the planner for holding the plan and do the subtraction before you open it.

Notion template.does_well: Provides a structured place to hold work, with fields and views already laid out.
Notion template.does_not: Run anything. A template is a container and containers stay empty at exactly the moments they would help.
Notion template.choose_when: You have a working process and want it represented somewhere durable and shared.
Notion template.differs: A template is a shape for state. The operating question is what happens on the day nobody opens it.
Notion template.mistaken_for: A process. A template is a shape for state; the process is what puts things in it.
Notion template.wrong_metric: How complete the setup looks, which peaks before any real use.
Notion template.first_week: Use the template for one real week without customising it.
Notion template.stack: Hold state in the template and keep the rules about what happens daily as text you can paste.

accountability app.does_well: Adds an external check and sometimes a social or financial cost to missing.
accountability app.does_not: Change what happens on the day you miss, other than by making the miss more expensive.
accountability app.choose_when: External stakes reliably help you and the commitment is correctly sized already.
accountability app.differs: Raising the cost of a miss also raises the cost of looking, and not looking is the failure mode that ends most accountability structures.
accountability app.mistaken_for: Accountability. It supplies a consequence; accountability is the comparison that precedes it.
accountability app.wrong_metric: Stakes size, which raises the cost of looking as fast as the cost of missing.
accountability app.first_week: Run the comparison with no stakes attached for one week and see whether it survives.
accountability app.stack: Use the app for the external check and keep the commitment writing separate from it.

online course.does_well: Transfers a body of knowledge in a designed order, with someone else having done the sequencing.
online course.does_not: Operate in your week. Knowing the method and running the method are different problems.
online course.choose_when: The gap is genuinely knowledge rather than execution.
online course.differs: A course ends. An operating system is the part that has to still be running in month four.
online course.mistaken_for: An execution fix. It transfers knowledge, which is a different constraint.
online course.wrong_metric: Completion percentage, which measures consumption rather than change.
online course.first_week: Take the one idea you would actually run and run it before continuing the course.
online course.stack: Take the method from the course and put the running of it in a daily loop.

human executive coach.does_well: Brings judgment, accountability with a real relationship attached, and the ability to notice what you are not saying.
human executive coach.does_not: Exist at 6am on a Tuesday when the decision is in front of you.
human executive coach.choose_when: The problem needs judgment, challenge, or a perspective genuinely outside your own.
human executive coach.differs: These are not substitutes. A structure that runs daily and a person who meets you fortnightly do different jobs, and the honest comparison is about which job is currently unmet.
human executive coach.escalate: If what you need is a professional relationship with someone who knows your situation, that is a person, not a prompt.
human executive coach.mistaken_for: An alternative to a structure. They do different jobs and both are frequently needed.
human executive coach.wrong_metric: Sessions per month, which says nothing about the days between them.
human executive coach.first_week: Write down what you would want from a session, then check whether it needs a person or a rule.
human executive coach.stack: Use the sessions for judgment and challenge, and a written loop for the days between them.

therapy.does_well: Provides clinical support for mental health, delivered by a qualified professional within a professional standard of care.
therapy.does_not: Overlap with an execution structure in any meaningful way. It is a different category of thing entirely.
therapy.choose_when: The question involves your mental health. That is not a comparison; it is the answer.
therapy.differs: This page does not position an educational productivity system as an alternative to therapy, because it is not one.
therapy.escalate: Nothing on this page is a diagnosis, a treatment, or a substitute for professional care. If you are in distress, contact a qualified professional or a local emergency service.
therapy.mistaken_for: Something a productivity system could substitute for. It cannot, and this page does not claim otherwise.
therapy.wrong_metric: Any comparison at all. These are different categories and comparing them produces nothing useful.
therapy.first_week: If the question is about your mental health, the next step is a qualified professional rather than any product.
therapy.stack: There is no stack here. Work commitments can be organized around care; they are not a form of it.

productivity app.does_well: Captures, sorts, and surfaces items, usually faster and more reliably than paper.
productivity app.does_not: Decide what belongs on the list or what to do when the list exceeds the day.
productivity app.choose_when: Capture and retrieval are the bottleneck.
productivity app.differs: Most productivity problems are decision problems wearing a storage problem's clothes, and better storage does not touch them.
productivity app.mistaken_for: A decision system. It stores and surfaces; it does not decide.
productivity app.wrong_metric: Capture speed, which is rarely the bottleneck it is optimized for.
productivity app.first_week: Stop adding to it for a week and see whether anything actually breaks.
productivity app.stack: Capture in the app and keep the rules about what happens to the list somewhere you read daily.

bullet journal.does_well: Keeps planning slow, manual, and physical, which for many people makes it more considered.
bullet journal.does_not: Carry structure between days on its own; the migration step is manual and is where it usually stops.
bullet journal.choose_when: The friction of writing by hand is a feature rather than a cost for you.
bullet journal.differs: The value is in the deliberateness of the writing. What it does not supply is a rule for the day the writing does not happen.
bullet journal.mistaken_for: A system that carries itself. The migration step is manual and is where it usually stops.
bullet journal.wrong_metric: How good the pages look, which is unrelated to whether the work moved.
bullet journal.first_week: Do the migration on a day you do not feel like it, and note what that cost.
bullet journal.stack: Keep the writing by hand and put the rule for missed days in the front of the book.

mastermind.does_well: Provides peer perspective, a recurring external commitment, and exposure to how other people solve the same problem.
mastermind.does_not: Operate between sessions, which is where the week actually happens.
mastermind.choose_when: Isolation is the constraint and you would benefit from being asked about it by peers.
mastermind.differs: A fortnightly external check and a daily internal loop are complements, not alternatives.
mastermind.mistaken_for: Ongoing accountability. It is a recurring external check with two weeks of silence around it.
mastermind.wrong_metric: How useful the last session felt, which is set by the conversation rather than the fortnight.
mastermind.first_week: Write what you will report at the next session and run the fortnight against that.
mastermind.stack: Use the group for perspective and a daily loop for the days it does not meet.

chief of staff.does_well: Converts ambiguity into actions, sequences priorities, and holds context you do not have room for.
chief of staff.does_not: Come cheaply, or exist at all for most people asking this question.
chief of staff.choose_when: The volume genuinely justifies a person, and you can define the role well enough to hire for it.
chief of staff.differs: The conversion work is the part that can be systematized. Judgment and relationships are the parts that cannot.
chief of staff.mistaken_for: A solution most people asking this question can buy. Usually they cannot.
chief of staff.wrong_metric: Volume handed off, which measures delegation rather than whether the pile is convertible.
chief of staff.first_week: Do one conversion pass yourself to see what the role would actually be doing.
chief of staff.stack: Systematize the conversion work and reserve a person for judgment and relationships.

calendar app.does_well: Holds commitments against time and tells you about collisions.
calendar app.does_not: Say whether the commitments fit, or what to drop when they do not.
calendar app.choose_when: The problem is knowing when things are, not deciding what they should be.
calendar app.differs: A calendar accepts an over-committed day without objection. The subtraction that makes a day possible happens outside it.
calendar app.mistaken_for: A plan. It records commitments and has no view on whether they fit.
calendar app.wrong_metric: How full the calendar is, which is highest in the weeks nothing gets finished.
calendar app.first_week: Block the first hour of every day and treat it as an external commitment.
calendar app.stack: Keep commitments in the calendar and do the fit arithmetic before anything is booked.

to-do list.does_well: Holds items so they do not have to be remembered, which is genuinely most of the value.
to-do list.does_not: Distinguish an item that is a task from an item that is an unmade decision, and lists fill with the second kind.
to-do list.choose_when: Capture is the problem and the items are already well formed.
to-do list.differs: The question is what happens to the items that get read three times and never started.
to-do list.mistaken_for: A list of tasks. Most lists are a mix of tasks and unmade decisions.
to-do list.wrong_metric: Items completed, which favors a day of small things over a day that moved one real thing.
to-do list.first_week: Mark every item you read twice without starting; those are the decisions.
to-do list.stack: Hold items in the list and run a conversion pass on the marked ones weekly.

journaling system.does_well: Creates a record of thinking and a place to process it, on your own terms and at your own pace.
journaling system.does_not: Produce a next action, and is not designed to.
journaling system.choose_when: Processing is what you need, which is often.
journaling system.differs: Reflection and execution are different activities, and combining them tends to weaken both.
journaling system.mistaken_for: An execution tool. Processing and execution are different activities.
journaling system.wrong_metric: Words written, which is a measure of processing rather than movement.
journaling system.first_week: Keep journaling and add one line at the end naming a next action, or explicitly none.
journaling system.stack: Process in the journal and keep the daily loop separate so neither weakens the other.

coaching retainer.does_well: Buys ongoing access to a person's judgment and a standing external commitment.
coaching retainer.does_not: Change the ninety per cent of the month you are not in a session.
coaching retainer.choose_when: You will use the access, and the gap is judgment rather than structure.
coaching retainer.differs: The honest question is what runs between sessions, and that question is not answered by the retainer.
coaching retainer.escalate: Verify credentials, scope, and boundaries directly with any provider before committing.
coaching retainer.mistaken_for: Coverage. You are buying access, and access has to be used to be worth anything.
coaching retainer.wrong_metric: Retainer cost per session, which ignores the ninety per cent of the month between them.
coaching retainer.first_week: Write what you will bring to the next session and what will run without it.
coaching retainer.stack: Use the retainer for judgment and a written structure for the rest of the month.

AI prompt pack.does_well: Supplies phrasings that reliably produce a particular kind of output.
AI prompt pack.does_not: Say when to use which one, or what happens on the day none of them is opened.
AI prompt pack.choose_when: You know what you want and need the phrasing.
AI prompt pack.differs: A pack is a set of prompts. The operating layer is the rules about which prompt fires when, and that is the part that is usually missing.
AI prompt pack.mistaken_for: An operating system. A pack is a set of phrasings; the operating layer is which one fires when.
AI prompt pack.wrong_metric: Number of prompts, which grows fastest in packs nobody opens.
AI prompt pack.first_week: Use three prompts for a week and delete the rest from view.
AI prompt pack.stack: Keep the pack for phrasing and write the rules about when each one is used.

generic ChatGPT chat.does_well: Answers what you asked, in a fresh context, with no setup at all.
generic ChatGPT chat.does_not: Carry your constraints, standards, or history unless you type them again.
generic ChatGPT chat.choose_when: You need one answer now and will not need this repeatedly.
generic ChatGPT chat.differs: The difference is not capability. It is whether the constraints arrive with the question or have to be remembered each time.
generic ChatGPT chat.mistaken_for: The whole capability. It is the capability with no setup attached.
generic ChatGPT chat.wrong_metric: How good today's answer was, which does not predict tomorrow's in this mode.
generic ChatGPT chat.first_week: Count the times you retype the same context. Three is the threshold to install something.
generic ChatGPT chat.stack: Use it for one-off answers and paste a rules block when the same request recurs.

Claude Project.does_well: Holds documents and instructions alongside a conversation so context does not have to be repasted.
Claude Project.does_not: Decide which of your rules should be standing and which are today's noise.
Claude Project.choose_when: You want stored context in one product and are comfortable with that product holding it.
Claude Project.differs: Stored context is a convenience over a portable rules block. Keep the portable version so the setup survives changing products.
Claude Project.mistaken_for: A portable setup. Stored context is convenient and lives inside one product.
Claude Project.wrong_metric: How much context is stored, which is not the same as how much of it is current.
Claude Project.first_week: Read the stored instructions in full. If you cannot, they are too long to be doing their job.
Claude Project.stack: Keep the portable rules block as the source of truth and let the project hold a copy.

Gemini chat.does_well: Answers in a conversational context with access to the surrounding product ecosystem.
Gemini chat.does_not: Supply the operating rules; those still have to come from you.
Gemini chat.choose_when: You are already working inside that ecosystem and the integration saves real steps.
Gemini chat.differs: Integration reduces friction. It does not decide what the day is for.
Gemini chat.mistaken_for: A workflow. Integration removes steps; it does not decide what the day is for.
Gemini chat.wrong_metric: Number of integrations enabled, which is a measure of surface rather than usefulness.
Gemini chat.first_week: Write down what the integration is allowed to see before enabling anything.
Gemini chat.stack: Use the integration for retrieval and keep the operating rules as text.

Perplexity thread.does_well: Answers questions with sources attached, which makes checking the answer cheap.
Perplexity thread.does_not: Run a daily loop; it is built for retrieval rather than for execution structure.
Perplexity thread.choose_when: The question is factual and you want to verify the answer.
Perplexity thread.differs: Retrieval and execution are different jobs. Use it for the first and something else for the second.
Perplexity thread.mistaken_for: An execution tool. It is built for retrieval, and retrieval is a different job.
Perplexity thread.wrong_metric: Number of sources cited, which does not tell you whether the question was the right one.
Perplexity thread.first_week: Use it for the factual half of one decision and note where the framing had to come from you.
Perplexity thread.stack: Check facts here and run the loop elsewhere.

ChatGPT.context_note: Conversation context lives in the thread, and separate threads do not see each other unless you say so.
ChatGPT.setup_note: Paste the rules block at the top of a new thread each day rather than extending yesterday's.
ChatGPT.caveat: Interface details, memory behavior, and tier features change. Keep the rules as pasteable text so nothing depends on a button existing.
ChatGPT.first_move: Open a fresh thread, paste the rules block at the top, and do the day's work below it rather than extending yesterday's thread.
ChatGPT.wrong_move: Building the workflow around a memory or projects feature. It is convenient and it is not inspectable, so drift in it is invisible.
ChatGPT.mistaken_for: A place where your setup lives. Nothing lives in a thread beyond the thread.
ChatGPT.wrong_metric: How long the current thread is, which correlates with accumulated contradiction rather than context.
ChatGPT.first_week: Start each day in a new thread seeded from the rules block and note what re-seeding actually costs.
ChatGPT.seeding: Paste the whole rules block as the first message of a fresh thread. If that is too long to do daily, the block is too long.
ChatGPT.state_note: Treat anything the product remembers between sessions as a cache. The pasteable block stays the source of truth.

Claude.context_note: Long documents can sit alongside the conversation, so the rules block can be a file rather than a paste.
Claude.setup_note: Keep the rules file short enough to read in full, and version it so you can tell which version produced a session.
Claude.caveat: Stored context is a convenience. Keep a plain-text copy so the setup survives a product change.
Claude.first_move: Put the rules in a file that sits alongside the conversation, and give the file a version marker so a behavior change can be attributed to an edit.
Claude.wrong_move: Letting the file grow. A rules document too long to read in full stops being read, and then it stops being the source of truth.
Claude.mistaken_for: A place to store everything. Long context makes it easy to keep material that has expired.
Claude.wrong_metric: How much you have attached, which is not the same as how much of it is current.
Claude.first_week: Read the attached rules document in full once. If you will not, it is too long to be governing anything.
Claude.seeding: Keep the rules in a short document alongside the conversation, with a version marker at the top.
Claude.state_note: Documents persist and drift silently. Put the review date in the document itself.

Gemini.context_note: Sits inside a wider product ecosystem, so some steps can be shortened by integration.
Gemini.setup_note: Decide deliberately what the integration is allowed to see, and write that decision down before you rely on it.
Gemini.caveat: Integration convenience is not portable. Anything load-bearing should also work from a pasted block.
Gemini.first_move: Decide what the integration is allowed to see, write that decision down, and only then wire anything to it.
Gemini.wrong_move: Accepting the default integration scope because it is convenient. Scope decided by a default is scope you did not decide.
Gemini.mistaken_for: A workflow because it connects to things. Connection removes steps; it does not decide anything.
Gemini.wrong_metric: Number of connected surfaces, which measures reach rather than usefulness.
Gemini.first_week: Write down what the integration may see before you enable it, and check the setting matches.
Gemini.seeding: Paste the rules block explicitly rather than assuming the surrounding context supplies it.
Gemini.state_note: Integration scope is a decision. A default is a scope you did not choose.

Perplexity.context_note: Optimized for retrieval with sources, which suits checking a claim more than running a loop.
Perplexity.setup_note: Use it for the factual half of a decision, and keep the execution loop elsewhere.
Perplexity.caveat: A sourced answer is still an answer to the question you asked. The framing is yours to get right.
Perplexity.first_move: Use it for the factual half of the question, then take the answer into whatever runs your execution loop.
Perplexity.wrong_move: Running a daily operating loop in a retrieval tool. It will answer, and the answers will not accumulate into anything.
Perplexity.mistaken_for: A general operating surface. It is optimized for retrieval with sources.
Perplexity.wrong_metric: Number of sources returned, which does not tell you whether the framing was right.
Perplexity.first_week: Use it for the factual half of one real decision and notice where you had to supply the framing.
Perplexity.seeding: Seed only what the retrieval needs. The operating rules belong wherever the loop runs.
Perplexity.state_note: Assume nothing carries between questions and write down anything you want to keep.

DeepSeek.context_note: A general assistant context with no assumptions about your setup.
DeepSeek.setup_note: Seed the rules block explicitly at the start; assume nothing carries over.
DeepSeek.caveat: Verify current terms, data handling, and availability with the provider before putting anything sensitive in.
DeepSeek.first_move: Seed the rules block explicitly at the start of every session and assume nothing carries over between them.
DeepSeek.wrong_move: Putting sensitive material in before reading the provider's current data handling terms. That decision belongs before the first session, not during one.
DeepSeek.mistaken_for: A drop-in replacement. It is a general assistant surface with its own terms and behavior.
DeepSeek.wrong_metric: Cost per use, which ignores what you have to verify before putting anything sensitive in.
DeepSeek.first_week: Read the current data handling terms before the first session, not during one.
DeepSeek.seeding: Seed the full rules block at the start of every session and assume nothing carries over.
DeepSeek.state_note: Verify availability, terms, and data handling with the provider; none of that is stable enough to assume.

three-chat setup.purpose: Separate standing rules, disposable daily runtime, and rule changes.
three-chat setup.trigger: A single long thread has started giving answers based on an expired version of your situation.
three-chat setup.output: Three named chats and a rules block short enough to paste in one action.
three-chat setup.failure: The runtime chat is kept for weeks and quietly becomes the rules chat.
three-chat setup.first_week: Discard the runtime chat every evening, even the ones that went well.

daily agenda trigger.purpose: Turn constraints and goals into a plan that fits the hours that exist.
daily agenda trigger.trigger: The start of the working day, before anything else is opened.
daily agenda trigger.output: A short ordered list allocated only against workable hours, plus an explicit deferred list.
daily agenda trigger.failure: It runs after the inbox is open, at which point the queue has already set the plan.
daily agenda trigger.first_week: Run it before opening anything else, and write the workable-hours number first.

end-of-day check-in.purpose: Close the day on evidence rather than on impression.
end-of-day check-in.trigger: The end of the working day, on good days and bad ones equally.
end-of-day check-in.output: Complete, partial with stopping point, missed, and one sentence naming tomorrow's first output.
end-of-day check-in.failure: It gets skipped on the bad days, which are the only days it would have told you anything.
end-of-day check-in.first_week: Run it in under three minutes so it survives a day you do not want to look at.

executive review mode.purpose: Organize what you already know into a decision without adding new material.
executive review mode.trigger: A decision that has been open long enough to have been rehearsed more than twice.
executive review mode.output: A decision in one sentence, or one named fact that would settle it and how you will get it.
executive review mode.failure: New information gets imported mid-session and the pass ends with a bigger pile and no decision.
executive review mode.first_week: Finish every pass with either a decision or one named fact that would settle it.

high-pressure coaching mode.purpose: Withdraw reassurance in the narrow case where reassurance is maintaining the loop.
high-pressure coaching mode.trigger: The same stuck situation described a third time with no action between the tellings.
high-pressure coaching mode.output: A physical action with a time attached, and a check-in at that time.
high-pressure coaching mode.failure: It becomes the default mode, at which point it stops carrying any information.
high-pressure coaching mode.first_week: Use it once, on the one loop that has genuinely repeated three times.

minimum viable day protocol.purpose: Keep a low-capacity day non-zero without pretending it is a normal day.
minimum viable day protocol.trigger: An honest read that the normal plan is not going to happen today.
minimum viable day protocol.output: One output with a written finished state, an explicit deferral list, and a stop condition.
minimum viable day protocol.failure: The declared small day turns into a normal day, which teaches you the small day was not real.
minimum viable day protocol.first_week: Stop at the stop condition even when energy returns.

privacy-safe setup.purpose: Decide in advance what does and does not go into a tool you do not control.
privacy-safe setup.trigger: Before the first session, not during one.
privacy-safe setup.output: A written category list: what goes in, what stays out, and where the out-of-scope material lives instead.
privacy-safe setup.failure: The categories get decided mid-session, under the pressure of wanting to explain something fully.
privacy-safe setup.first_week: Write both lists before the next session and keep them visible while you type.

context reset recovery.purpose: Recover when the working context has drifted from your actual situation.
context reset recovery.trigger: Corrections are taking longer than restating the situation would.
context reset recovery.output: A fresh context seeded from the rules block, with the old thread closed rather than continued.
context reset recovery.failure: The old thread gets continued 'just to finish this', and the drift comes with it.
context reset recovery.first_week: Close the drifted thread rather than correcting it, and re-seed from the rules block.

prompt pack installation.purpose: Turn instructions that work into instructions that apply without being remembered.
prompt pack installation.trigger: The third time you retype substantially the same instruction.
prompt pack installation.output: A single pasteable block with a version marker that passes a cold test in a fresh context.
prompt pack installation.failure: The pack grows until it is too long to paste, and then it stops being pasted.
prompt pack installation.first_week: Run the cold test in a fresh context and cut whatever turns out not to be load-bearing.

weekly review protocol.purpose: Read the week from the record rather than from memory.
weekly review protocol.trigger: A fixed time each week, kept even in weeks that felt bad.
weekly review protocol.output: One conclusion and one change to next week's commitments.
weekly review protocol.failure: It becomes a long reflective write-up, which makes it skippable in the weeks it matters.
weekly review protocol.first_week: Read the record, write one conclusion, change one thing, and stop.

legit.question: Is this a real product with a defined scope, or a repackaged list of tips?
legit.answer: It is a written system of named frameworks, modes, and boundaries, delivered as text you install into an assistant you already use. The scope is educational and organizational.
legit.check: Read the framework names and the boundaries before buying. A system that will not tell you what it refuses to do is not describing its scope.
legit.mistaken_for: A question about reviews. Reviews are the easiest thing to fake and the least useful thing to check.
legit.wrong_metric: Testimonial count, which is uncorrelated with whether the product suits you.
legit.first_week: Read what the product refuses to do before reading what it promises.
legit.what_it_is_not: It is not certified, accredited, or clinically validated, and it does not claim to be.
legit.evidence_to_ask_for: A plain statement of what you receive, in what format, and what the product will not do.

real.question: Does the thing described actually exist, or is the page the product?
real.answer: The product is a prompt and protocol system delivered on purchase. The pages describe the frameworks it contains.
real.check: Ask what you receive, in what format, and what happens if it does not suit you. Any product should answer those three plainly.
real.mistaken_for: A question about whether the site is real. The useful question is what arrives after payment.
real.wrong_metric: How polished the marketing is, which is cheap and tells you nothing about the contents.
real.first_week: Ask what the deliverable is and in what format before buying anything.
real.what_it_is_not: It is not software, a service, or an ongoing relationship. It is written material you install.
real.evidence_to_ask_for: A description of the deliverable specific enough that you would notice if it were absent.

a scam.question: Is there a hidden cost, a subscription trap, or an unverifiable claim?
a scam.answer: It is a one-off digital purchase handled through Gumroad. There are no outcome guarantees on these pages, and there should not be.
a scam.check: Treat any productivity product promising a specific result as making a claim it cannot support, including this one if it ever does.
a scam.mistaken_for: A question about the seller. It is better asked as a question about the claims.
a scam.wrong_metric: Price. Cheap products make unsupportable claims as readily as expensive ones.
a scam.first_week: Look for an outcome guarantee. Its presence is the warning sign, not its absence.
a scam.what_it_is_not: It is not a subscription, and it does not promise a specific result.
a scam.evidence_to_ask_for: The refund terms and the checkout provider, both stated before you pay.

therapy.question: Is this a substitute for therapy?
therapy.answer: No. It is educational and organizational, it does not diagnose or treat anything, and it is not delivered by a clinician.
therapy.check: If the question is about your mental health, the right comparison is between qualified professionals, not between a professional and a productivity system.
therapy.mistaken_for: A comparison. These are different categories and comparing them is not useful.
therapy.wrong_metric: Cost per month against a therapist's fee, which frames two unrelated things as substitutes.
therapy.first_week: If the question is about your mental health, the next step is a qualified professional.
therapy.what_it_is_not: It is not therapy, not delivered by a clinician, and not a treatment for anything.
therapy.evidence_to_ask_for: Nothing from this product. For care, the credentials to check are a clinician's.

a course.question: Is this a course I have to work through?
a course.answer: No. There is no curriculum and no completion. It is a set of instructions you install and then run.
a course.check: Ask whether the value is in learning it or in running it. Products differ, and the difference determines whether it survives month three.
a course.mistaken_for: A format question. The real question is whether your gap is knowledge or execution.
a course.wrong_metric: Hours of content, which measures how long it takes to consume rather than what changes.
a course.first_week: Decide honestly whether you already know what to do. If you do, more knowledge is not the purchase.
a course.what_it_is_not: It is not a curriculum, has no modules, and there is nothing to complete.
a course.evidence_to_ask_for: A statement of whether the value is in learning it or in running it.

worth it.question: Does the value justify the price for someone in my situation?
worth it.answer: That depends on whether your constraint is knowledge or execution. If you already know what to do and it is not happening, structure is the relevant purchase.
worth it.check: Write down what you would expect to be different in a month. If you cannot, no product will answer the question.
worth it.mistaken_for: A price question. Price is knowable; fit is the part that decides it.
worth it.wrong_metric: What other people got out of it, which depends on constraints that are not yours.
worth it.first_week: Write what you would expect to be different in a month. If you cannot, no product answers this.
worth it.what_it_is_not: It is not a guarantee of any outcome, and it does not claim to work for everyone.
worth it.evidence_to_ask_for: A clear statement of who it is not for.

safe to use.question: Is it safe to run this against my own decisions?
safe to use.answer: It is educational and organizational only. It carries explicit boundaries around health, legal, financial, and safety matters, and those boundaries are not optional.
safe to use.check: Any system that will advise you on all four of those categories without a boundary is one to be careful with.
safe to use.mistaken_for: A question about the software. It is a question about scope and boundaries.
safe to use.wrong_metric: How careful the language sounds, which is easy to produce and easy to abandon in practice.
safe to use.first_week: Read the boundaries section first and check that it names things the product refuses to do.
safe to use.what_it_is_not: It is not medical, legal, financial, or therapeutic advice, and it says so on every page.
safe to use.evidence_to_ask_for: An explicit list of the situations in which the product tells you to stop and get a professional.

private enough.question: What happens to what I type?
private enough.answer: That is determined by the assistant you use, not by this system. The system's own guidance is to decide categories in advance and keep sensitive material out.
private enough.check: Read the data handling terms of the assistant you plan to use. That is where the answer actually lives.
private enough.mistaken_for: A question about this product. What you type goes to whichever assistant you use.
private enough.wrong_metric: The product's own privacy claims, which do not govern the assistant you paste into.
private enough.first_week: Read the data handling terms of the assistant you plan to use, then decide your categories.
private enough.what_it_is_not: It is not a hosted service and it does not receive, store, or process what you type into an assistant.
private enough.evidence_to_ask_for: The assistant provider's current terms, which is where the answer actually lives.

for non-founders.question: Does this only apply to founders?
for non-founders.answer: The frameworks are about capacity, ambiguity, drift, and ties, which are not founder-specific. The examples lean founder because that is who the product was written for first.
for non-founders.check: Read one framework and ask whether its trigger describes a situation you are actually in.
for non-founders.mistaken_for: A question about the marketing. The examples lean founder; the frameworks are about capacity and ambiguity.
for non-founders.wrong_metric: Whether the copy speaks to you, which is a writing question rather than a fit one.
for non-founders.first_week: Read one framework's trigger and ask whether it describes a situation you are actually in.
for non-founders.what_it_is_not: It is not role-specific, and it is also not written to be universal.
for non-founders.evidence_to_ask_for: The list of framework triggers, so you can check them against your own week.

better than a productivity app.question: Why not just use an app?
better than a productivity app.answer: They do different jobs. An app stores and surfaces items; this is a set of rules about what to do with them. Most people who need the second already own the first.
better than a productivity app.check: Ask whether your problem is that you lose track of things or that you know what to do and it does not happen.
better than a productivity app.mistaken_for: A feature comparison. They do different jobs and most people who need one already own the other.
better than a productivity app.wrong_metric: Feature count, which compares a storage tool with a set of rules as if they competed.
better than a productivity app.first_week: Decide whether your problem is losing track of things or knowing what to do and not doing it.
better than a productivity app.what_it_is_not: It is not an app, stores nothing, and integrates with nothing.
better than a productivity app.evidence_to_ask_for: A statement of what it does not do, which for this category is most of what an app does.

framework_selection.note: Ranked lists of frameworks that genuinely address each axis value. The page's secondary axis selects a position in the list, so adjacent pages are anchored to different frameworks rather than all inheriting the first concept in the table.

comparison_policy.note: A category has no official source, so a category comparison cannot satisfy the comparison_graph lane honestly. Those pages are generated in category_comparison, which requires more words and forbids product-specific claims, rather than citing a search URL as if it were an official source.
